requirement:
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
rationale:
**Verdict:** the implementation follows every obligation in `outline_comments`, the `{impl}` marking is complete, and the tests cover the rules and their boundaries. One contrived edge case (below) is a residual limitation that I did not count as a gap.

**Implementation**

- **Profiles define comments.**
  - `Profile.is_comment` is set per profile in `src/outline/{rust,python,css,toml,yaml,typescript,markdown}.rs`.
  - The Markdown profile treats only `html_block` nodes that begin with `<!--` and end with `-->` as comments (`markdown.rs::is_comment`). An inline HTML comment is therefore paragraph text of its section.
- **Runs.** `assign_comments` (`src/outline/mod.rs`) joins comments into a run only when all of these hold:
  - neither comment follows code on its line (`trails_code`);
  - only whitespace lies between them;
  - the next comment starts on the same line as the previous one ends, or on the next line;
  - both comments have the same `binds_to_container` value.

  A comment that follows code, including one that follows another comment, forms a run by itself.

  Splitting a run when a container-bound comment meets an ordinary one is my reading of the "MAY bind a comment kind to its container" clause. It is a reasonable reading, and it is what makes `//! Module docs.` followed by `// above inner` give the owners the tests expect.
- **Trailing runs.** `trailing_owner` descends to the innermost node whose pre-widening line range covers the line. Among siblings sharing the line, it picks the last one that starts before the comment.
- **Other runs.** `run_owner` finds the smallest containing node, then takes the first child that starts at or after the run's end. If there is no such child, the container owns the run, and the root is the container at top level.
- **Container binding.** `rust.rs::is_inner_doc_comment`, wired as `comment_binds_to_container`, makes `//!` and `/*!` runs belong to the smallest containing node. A file-level inner doc comment therefore belongs to the root. All other profiles use `never`.
- **References count for the owning node.**
  - `Outline::owner_at_line` and `comment_owners_at_line` (`src/outline/mod.rs`) feed `reference_selector` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs`, which carries out the `authoring_inputs` part.
  - `rust_coverage.rs::missing_function_references` credits each comment's reference to `comment.owner`, which carries out the `rust_item_coverage` part. I assessed these only as context, as instructed.
  - `nodes_for_lines` and `nodes_for_range` give the search tool comment-owner semantics.
- **Marking.** The functions, structs and profiles that implement the rules carry `{impl}` references, including the helpers `trails_code`, `trailing_owner`, `run_owner`, `record_comment`, `record_comments_within` and `walk`.

**Residual limitation (not counted as a gap)**

Source references are located by line only (`SourceReference.line`), so `owner_at_line` returns the first comment owner on a line. If two comments with different owners share one line, a reference in the second comment would be attributed to the first comment's owner. For example, `/* a */ /* {impl}… */` after a function: the first comment's owner is the next node, and the second's is the root. This needs a contrived layout and is not covered by a test. I judged it minor.

**Tests**

- `src/outline/tests.rs`:
  - `comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container` covers a run before a node, a trailing comment, a floating comment, a blank line between a run and its node, inner doc comments in the root and in a module, a comment alone in a container, a final top-level comment, and the widening of the owner's line ranges.
  - `comment_between_two_fns_belongs_to_the_next`, `trailing_comment_after_last_fn_in_mod_belongs_to_the_mod` and `top_level_comment_with_nothing_after_belongs_to_the_root` cover the next-node, container and root fallbacks.
  - `comment_after_code_on_a_line_belongs_to_that_lines_node` covers trailing comments at several nesting depths.
  - `file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root` covers `//!` and `/*!`.
  - `comment_runs_follow_the_same_rules_in_every_language` covers Python, TypeScript, TSX, CSS, TOML, YAML and Markdown.
  - `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` covers the inline versus block distinction.
  - `a_comment_after_another_comment_on_its_line_forms_its_own_run` covers a comment that follows another comment on its line.
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs::references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes` checks that references contribute their owning outline nodes (a Markdown section, a plain-text file, and a Rust module).
- `src/authoring/tools.rs::search_returns_innermost_nodes_and_comment_owners` checks that a search hit inside a comment returns the comment's owner.

No gaps are acknowledged by FIXME comments.

profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file in the project: every `.rs` file except those under `.git` or `target` directories at any depth or under the project-root `book`, `evidence`, or `vendor` directories. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When authoring evidence, the edges defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.targets` MUST determine the reference
contributions to the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`. The target of each edge leaving
the assessed subject MUST contribute; sources with only edges into the subject
MUST NOT contribute and remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. A `{cite}` made by the subject
contributes the cited definition's complete fenced declaration. An anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` contributes the complete anchored file.
An in-source `{impl}` or `{test}` reference to the subject contributes the source
containing it: for a reference in a supported language, the smallest enclosing
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; for a reference in a Markdown requirement, example, or
terminology declaration, that complete declaration; for other references, the
complete containing source file. Literal references, evidence copies, and
generated output MUST remain excluded under the existing reference-discovery
rules.
These contribution rules MUST apply only to edges directly leaving the assessed
subject. Including another declaration or source MUST NOT by itself recursively
expand that source's own edges. Reference links MUST NOT be described as proof
that all substantively relevant sources have been found.
